subtopics.title: The Pulse — a Single Disturbance That Travels

questions.question: Which of these is a pulse?
options: A single disturbance travelling through a medium
A repeating train of crests and troughs
The stretched spring before anything moves
Any object that vibrates in place

questions.question: A pulse is called transverse when the particles of the medium move:
options: Parallel to the direction the pulse travels
Perpendicular — at right angles — to the direction the pulse travels
In the same direction as the energy transfer
Around the spring in circles

questions.question: A piece of tape is stuck to one coil of a spring. After several pulses have passed, the tape is found:
options: Several coils closer to the far end
At the far end of the spring
Exactly where it started — each particle only makes a short round trip while energy travels on
Permanently lifted above the rest line

questions.question: A pulse travels 8 m along a spring in 4 s. A much smaller pulse launched on the same stretched spring travels at:
options: A slower speed, because it carries less energy
8 m·s⁻¹
2 m·s⁻¹ — the medium sets the speed, not the size of the pulse
4 m·s⁻¹

subtopics.title: Amplitude, and What the Medium Actually Does

questions.question: Amplitude is defined as the:
options: Width of the hump along the spring
Distance from a trough to a crest
Total length of the disturbed spring
Maximum displacement of a particle of the medium from its rest position

questions.question: A dip reaches 0,25 m below the rest line. The displacement at its lowest point, and the amplitude, are:
options: Displacement minus 0,25 m; amplitude 0,25 m
Displacement plus 0,25 m; amplitude minus 0,25 m
Both minus 0,25 m
Displacement zero; amplitude 0,25 m

questions.question: A 0,4 m pulse and a 0,05 m pulse are launched together on the same spring. They:
options: Arrive together — amplitude records energy, but speed belongs to the medium
Arrive with the big pulse well ahead
Arrive with the small pulse well ahead
Cannot travel on the same spring

questions.question: A pulse moving at 2 m·s⁻¹ must cover 5 m. The time needed is:
options: 2,5 s — time equals distance divided by speed, 5 ÷ 2
5 s

questions.question: Where two pulses occupy the same point at the same time, the displacement of the medium equals the:
options: Displacement of whichever pulse arrived first
Difference between the two amplitudes, ignoring signs
Algebraic sum of the individual displacements — added with their signs
Average of the two displacements

questions.question: A crest of plus 0,4 m overlaps a crest of plus 0,2 m. The displacement of the medium at that instant is:
options: 0,6 m — plus 0,4 plus 0,2

questions.question: A crest of plus 0,4 m overlaps a trough of minus 0,1 m. The displacement of the medium at that instant is:
options: Plus 0,5 m
Minus 0,3 m
Zero
Plus 0,3 m — the algebraic sum of plus 0,4 and minus 0,1

questions.question: Once two overlapping pulses separate again, each pulse:
options: Continues completely unchanged — original shape, amplitude and direction
Travels on with reduced amplitude
Reflects back toward where it came from
Is permanently absorbed by the other

questions.question: Constructive interference happens when two pulses:
options: Displace the medium in opposite directions
Travel at different speeds
Displace the medium in the same direction, so the resultant is larger than either pulse
Have exactly equal amplitudes

questions.question: Two troughs of minus 0,15 m each overlap completely. The resultant displacement is:
options: Zero — they cancel
Minus 0,15 m
Plus 0,3 m
Minus 0,3 m — constructive interference, because both disturbances point the same way

questions.question: A crest of 0,3 m meets a trough of minus 0,3 m. At complete overlap the spring is:
options: Momentarily flat — yet both pulses still exist and emerge unchanged
Flat forever, because the pulses destroyed each other
Displaced by 0,6 m
Oscillating at twice the frequency

questions.question: In destructive interference the resultant displacement is always:
options: Exactly zero
Smaller than the larger pulse — opposite displacements partly or wholly cancel
Larger than either pulse
Equal to the sum of the sizes, ignoring signs

subtopics.title: One Flick of the Washing Line

questions.question: While the hump runs along the washing line, a peg on the line:
options: Hops straight up and settles back exactly where it hung
Slides along with the hump to the far pole
Twists around the line
Moves backward toward your hand

questions.question: To make humps travel faster along the washing line you must:
options: Snap your wrist harder
Change the line itself — for example, winch it tighter
Send taller humps
Send humps more often

questions.question: A hump crosses the 10 m yard in 5 s. What actually arrives at the far pole?
options: The line and the pegs
Nothing measurable
The disturbance and the energy of your flick, travelling at 2 metres every second
A piece of the line moving at 2 metres every second

subtopics.title: When Two Bumps Meet in the Middle

questions.question: Your 25 cm hump meets your friend's 15 cm hump. At full overlap the rope stands at:
options: 25 cm
10 cm
40 cm — the rope adds both heights
15 cm

questions.question: Immediately after the two humps meet, they:
options: Merge permanently into one 40 cm hump
Pass through each other and carry on, each unchanged
Bounce back toward their senders
Shrink to half size each

questions.question: The two scenes of every pulse-meeting story are:
options: Overlap: the bigger hump swallows the smaller; after: one hump remains
Overlap: both stop; after: both restart slowly
Overlap: the heights swap; after: each goes home
Overlap: add the heights; after: both pulses continue unchanged

questions.question: An up-flick of plus 30 cm meets a down-flick of minus 10 cm. At full overlap the rope shows:
options: A bump of plus 20 cm — plus 30 minus 10
A tower of 40 cm
A dip of minus 20 cm
A flat line

questions.question: The one-line rule for naming interference is:
options: Tall pulses build, short pulses cancel
First pulse builds, second pulse cancels
Same signs build (constructive); opposite signs cancel (destructive)
Ups always overpower downs

questions.question: A 20 cm hump meets a 20 cm dip and the rope goes momentarily flat. This means:
options: The pulses have cancelled permanently
Both pulses are still there mid-crossing — each emerges whole a moment later
The energy has vanished from the rope
The rope has reached its elastic limit
